subproblems.title: Chain rule with Schwarz symmetry for the coefficient field DPsi(Du)
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) (= Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, operator norm) and Psi : L -> R of class C^2. Let U ⊆ R^n be open and u : R^n -> R^l of class C^2 on U. Then for every e in R^n and every y in U, D(z -> DPsi(Du(z)))(y)e = D^2Psi(Du(y))[Dv_e(y)] in L* = L(L, R), where v_e(z) := Du(z)e = fderiv R u z e and D^2Psi(P)[Q] := fderiv R (fderiv R Psi) P Q.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ n ℓ : ℕ, ∀ (Ψ : (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) → ℝ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (u : Rn n → Rn ℓ), IsOpen U → ContDiff ℝ 2 Ψ → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 u U → ∀ (e y : Rn n), y ∈ U → fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ Ψ (fderiv ℝ u z)) y e = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Ψ) (fderiv ℝ u y) (fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ u z e) y)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 1-2 of the parent proof of dohr_eb_ehs_differentiated_el (regularity of Du and DPsi o Du, chain rule, Schwarz symmetry), isolated as the pointwise identity (*) DF(y)e = B(Du(y))[Dv_e(y)].
Notation: L := L(R^n, R^l) = (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ), L* := L(L, R). A := DPsi = fderiv R Psi : L -> L*, B := DA = fderiv R (fderiv R Psi), so B(P)[Q] = fderiv R (fderiv R Psi) P Q in L*. Du := fderiv R u : R^n -> L and D^2u(y) := D(Du)(y) = fderiv R (fderiv R u) y in L(R^n, L), so D^2u(y)[w][e] = fderiv R (fderiv R u) y w e. F(z) := A(Du(z)) and v_e(z) := Du(z)e = fderiv R u z e. Fix e in R^n and y in U.
1. Regularity of Du. U is open and u is C^2 on U, so Du is C^1 on U (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen with 1 + 1 <= 2). As U is a neighbourhood of y, Du is differentiable at y with derivative D^2u(y).
2. Regularity of A. Psi is C^2 on L, so A = DPsi is C^1 on L (ContDiff.fderiv_right with 1 + 1 <= 2); in particular A is differentiable at Du(y) with derivative B(Du(y)).
3. Chain rule. By steps 1-2, F = A o Du is differentiable at y and DF(y) = B(Du(y)) o D^2u(y). Evaluating at e gives DF(y)e = B(Du(y))[D^2u(y)e], where D^2u(y)e in L is the linear map w -> D^2u(y)[e][w].
4. Derivative of v_e. v_e(z) = Du(z)e is the application of the C^1 operator field z -> Du(z) to the constant vector e. By the product rule for z -> c(z)(d(z)) with c = Du differentiable at y and d = e constant (fderiv_clm_apply; the term containing the derivative of the constant d is 0), v_e is differentiable at y and Dv_e(y)w = (D^2u(y)w)e = D^2u(y)[w][e] for every w in R^n; that is, Dv_e(y) = (D^2u(y)).flip e.
5. Schwarz symmetry. u is C^2 on the open neighbourhood U of y, hence C^2 at y (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt). Therefore its second derivative at y is symmetric (Schwarz's theorem; Mathlib ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt, whose hypothesis minSmoothness R 2 <= 2 holds since minSmoothness R 2 = 2 over the real field): D^2u(y)[w][e] = D^2u(y)[e][w] for all w, e in R^n.
6. Conclusion. By steps 4 and 5, for every w in R^n, Dv_e(y)w = D^2u(y)[w][e] = D^2u(y)[e][w] = (D^2u(y)e)w, so Dv_e(y) = D^2u(y)e as elements of L. Substituting this into step 3 gives DF(y)e = B(Du(y))[D^2u(y)e] = B(Du(y))[Dv_e(y)], i.e. fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ Ψ (fderiv ℝ u z)) y e = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Ψ) (fderiv ℝ u y) (fderiv ℝ (fun z => fderiv ℝ u z e) y). QED

subproblems.title: Uniform convergence of difference quotients of a C^1 map on compact sets
subproblems.statement: Let n be a natural number, E : Type (universe 0) a real normed space, U ⊆ R^n open, f : R^n -> E of class C^1 on U, K ⊆ U compact and e in R^n. Then h^{-1}(f(x + he) - f(x)) -> Df(x)e = fderiv R f x e uniformly for x in K as h -> 0 with h ≠ 0 (TendstoUniformlyOn along the filter 𝓝[≠] 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Type) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (f : Rn n → E) (U K : Set (Rn n)) (e : Rn n), IsOpen U → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → TendstoUniformlyOn (fun (h : ℝ) (x : Rn n) => h⁻¹ • (f (x + h • e) - f x)) (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x e) (𝓝[≠] 0) K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 7 (and Step 9(a)-(b)) of the parent proof of dohr_eb_ehs_differentiated_el: uniform convergence of difference quotients by the mean value inequality and Heine-Cantor. It is stated once for a C^1 map with values in an arbitrary real normed space E (a type in universe 0, as in the Lean statement) so that it serves both the left side (F = DPsi o Du with values in L* = (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) →L[ℝ] ℝ) and the right side (zeta with values in Rn ℓ).
1. Margin. K is compact and K ⊆ U with U open, so there is eps > 0 with K_eps := cthickening eps K = {z : dist(z, K) <= eps} ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). K_eps is compact (IsCompact.cthickening) and contains K.
2. Regularity. Since f is C^1 on the open set U, f is differentiable at every point of U and Df = fderiv R f is continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen). Hence Df is uniformly continuous on the compact set K_eps (Heine-Cantor; IsCompact.uniformContinuousOn_of_continuous).
3. Constants. Let eta > 0. By step 2 choose theta > 0 such that ||Df(w) - Df(x)|| < eta/(||e|| + 1) whenever w, x lie in K_eps and ||w - x|| < theta. Put r := min(eps, theta)/(||e|| + 1) > 0. The set {h : 0 < |h| < r} belongs to the filter 𝓝[≠] 0.
4. Geometry. Let 0 < |h| < r and x in K. Then ||he|| = |h| ||e|| <= |h| (||e|| + 1) < min(eps, theta). The closed ball B(x, ||he||) is convex, contains x and x + he, and is contained in B(x, eps) ⊆ K_eps ⊆ U (closedBall_subset_cthickening). Hence the segment [x, x + he] lies in K_eps, and each w on it satisfies ||w - x|| <= ||he|| < theta.
5. Mean value inequality. On the segment f is differentiable (it lies in U), and ||Df(w) - Df(x)|| <= eta/(||e|| + 1) by steps 3-4 (w and x are in K_eps). The mean value inequality relative to the fixed linear map Df(x) (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le') gives ||f(x + he) - f(x) - Df(x)(he)|| <= (eta/(||e|| + 1)) ||he||.
6. Division by h. Since h ≠ 0 and Df(x)(he) = h Df(x)e, we have Df(x)e - h^{-1}(f(x + he) - f(x)) = -h^{-1}(f(x + he) - f(x) - Df(x)(he)). Therefore ||h^{-1}(f(x + he) - f(x)) - Df(x)e|| <= |h|^{-1} (eta/(||e|| + 1)) |h| ||e|| = eta ||e||/(||e|| + 1) < eta.
7. Conclusion. For every eta > 0 the estimate of step 6 holds for all x in K and all h with 0 < |h| < r, i.e. eventually along 𝓝[≠] 0, uniformly in x in K. By the metric characterisation of uniform convergence (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff) this is exactly TendstoUniformlyOn (fun h x => h⁻¹ • (f (x + h • e) - f x)) (fun x => fderiv ℝ f x e) (𝓝[≠] 0) K. (The case e = 0 is included; then both sides vanish.) QED

subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) and L* := L(L, R) (operator norms). Let U ⊆ R^n be open, F : R^n -> L* of class C^1 on U, tau : R^n -> L continuous with compact support and tsupport tau ⊆ U, and e in R^n. Then ∫_U F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] dx -> -∫_U DF(x)e[tau(x)] dx as h -> 0 with h ≠ 0 (along 𝓝[≠] 0), where DF(x)e := fderiv R F x e.

Source: Steps 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 of the parent proof of dohr_eb_ehs_differentiated_el (translation of the shifted term and passage to the limit on the left side), with F := DPsi o Du and tau := Dzeta abstracted. The uniform convergence of Step 7 is supplied by the sibling dohr_eb_ehs_del_diffquot_uniform.
Notation: K := tsupport tau; Q_h(y) := h^{-1}(F(y + he) - F(y)) in L*; DF(y)e := fderiv R F y e in L*. Lebesgue measure on R^n is translation invariant.
1. Margin. K is compact (tau has compact support) and K ⊆ U with U open, so there is delta > 0 with K' := cthickening delta K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Put h0 := delta/(||e|| + 1) > 0; {h : |h| < h0} is a neighbourhood of 0. For |h| < h0 and y in K, dist(y + he, y) = |h| ||e|| < delta, so y + he lies in K' ⊆ U.
2. Basic facts. tau(y) = 0 for y not in K. F is continuous on U, and y -> DF(y)e is continuous on U (F is C^1 on the open U: ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, then evaluation at e). tau is continuous with compact support, hence bounded: ||tau(y)|| <= C_tau for all y. Since K is compact and y -> DF(y)e is continuous on K, ||DF(y)e|| <= C_D for y in K.
3. Uniform convergence (sibling). By dohr_eb_ehs_del_diffquot_uniform with E := L*, f := F, the open set U, the compact set K ⊆ U and the direction e: Q_h(y) -> DF(y)e uniformly for y in K as h -> 0, h ≠ 0.
4. The left side is minus an integral of Q_h. Fix h with 0 < |h| < h0.
   (a) The integrand x -> F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] vanishes for x outside U: then x is not in K, so tau(x) = 0; and x - he is not in K, since otherwise x = (x - he) + he would lie in K' ⊆ U by step 1. Hence its integral over U equals its integral over R^n (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
   (b) Integrability. y -> F(y)[tau(y)] is continuous on the compact set K (F is continuous on U ⊇ K, tau is continuous, evaluation is continuous) and vanishes off K, so it is integrable on R^n (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact, then IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero). Likewise y -> F(y + he)[tau(y)] is continuous on K (because y + he lies in K' ⊆ U for y in K) and vanishes off K, hence is integrable; its translate x -> F(x)[tau(x - he)] is then integrable by translation invariance (Integrable.comp_sub_right).
   (c) By linearity of F(x), F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] = h^{-1}(F(x)[tau(x)] - F(x)[tau(x - he)]). With (b), the integral over R^n of the left side equals h^{-1}(∫ F(x)[tau(x)] dx - ∫ F(x)[tau(x - he)] dx).
   (d) Translation invariance (substitute x = y + he; integral_add_right_eq_self): ∫ F(x)[tau(x - he)] dx = ∫ F(y + he)[tau(y)] dy.
   (e) By (c), (d) and the integrability in (b): ∫ F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] dx = h^{-1} ∫ (F(y)[tau(y)] - F(y + he)[tau(y)]) dy = -∫ Q_h(y)[tau(y)] dy. The last integrand vanishes off K, so together with (a):
       ∫_U F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] dx = -∫_K Q_h(y)[tau(y)] dy   for all 0 < |h| < h0.   (1)
5. The limit integral. y -> DF(y)e[tau(y)] vanishes on U \ K, so (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero, K ⊆ U, U measurable)
       ∫_U DF(x)e[tau(x)] dx = ∫_K DF(y)e[tau(y)] dy.   (2)
6. Passage to the limit on K. By step 3 there is a punctured neighbourhood of 0 on which ||Q_h(y) - DF(y)e|| < 1 for every y in K; for such h and y in K, ||Q_h(y)|| <= ||DF(y)e|| + 1 <= C_D + 1, hence |Q_h(y)[tau(y)]| <= ||Q_h(y)|| ||tau(y)|| <= (C_D + 1) C_tau. Moreover:
   - for 0 < |h| < h0 the function y -> Q_h(y)[tau(y)] is continuous on K (y + he lies in U for y in K), hence a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to the compact, measurable set K;
   - the constant (C_D + 1) C_tau is integrable on K, which has finite measure;
   - for every y in K, Q_h(y) -> DF(y)e (uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence), hence Q_h(y)[tau(y)] -> DF(y)e[tau(y)] (evaluation at tau(y) is a continuous linear map on L*).
   The filter 𝓝[≠] 0 is countably generated, so the dominated convergence theorem (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) gives
       ∫_K Q_h(y)[tau(y)] dy -> ∫_K DF(y)e[tau(y)] dy   as h -> 0, h ≠ 0.   (3)
   (Equivalently, as in the parent proof, for small h one has |∫_K (Q_h(y) - DF(y)e)[tau(y)] dy| <= |K| C_tau sup_{y in K} ||Q_h(y) - DF(y)e||, which tends to 0 by step 3.)
7. Conclusion. By (1) the function h -> ∫_U F(x)[h^{-1}(tau(x) - tau(x - he))] dx agrees, on the punctured neighbourhood {0 < |h| < h0} of 0, with h -> -∫_K Q_h(y)[tau(y)] dy, which by (3) and (2) tends to -∫_K DF(y)e[tau(y)] dy = -∫_U DF(x)e[tau(x)] dx. Hence the claimed limit (Filter.Tendsto.congr'). QED

Notation: Kz := tsupport zeta; phi_h(x) := h^{-1}(zeta(x) - zeta(x - he)); Dzeta(x)e := fderiv R zeta x e.
1. Margin. Kz is compact and Kz ⊆ U with U open, so there is delta > 0 with K' := cthickening delta Kz ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open); K' is compact (IsCompact.cthickening), hence closed and of finite Lebesgue measure. Put h0 := delta/(||e|| + 1) > 0.
2. Bounds. g is continuous on U ⊇ K' and K' is compact, so ||g(x)|| <= C_g for x in K'. The map x -> Dzeta(x)e is continuous (zeta is C^1), so ||Dzeta(x)e|| <= C_z for x in K'.
3. Rewriting. For all h and x, x - he = x + h(-e), so phi_h(x) = -h^{-1}(zeta(x + h(-e)) - zeta(x)), and Dzeta(x)e = -Dzeta(x)(-e) by linearity. Hence phi_h(x) - Dzeta(x)e = -(h^{-1}(zeta(x + h(-e)) - zeta(x)) - Dzeta(x)(-e)).
4. Uniform and pointwise convergence (sibling). zeta is C^1 on the open set R^n. Applying dohr_eb_ehs_del_diffquot_uniform with E := R^l, f := zeta, the open set R^n, the compact set K' and the direction -e, and using step 3: phi_h -> Dzeta(.)e uniformly on K' as h -> 0, h ≠ 0. Applying it with the compact set {x} in place of K': phi_h(x) -> Dzeta(x)e for every x in R^n.
5. Support. Let 0 < |h| < h0 and x outside K'. Then zeta(x) = 0 because x is not in Kz ⊆ K'; and zeta(x - he) = 0, since otherwise x - he would lie in Kz and dist(x, x - he) = |h| ||e|| < delta would give x in K'. Hence phi_h(x) = 0.
6. Domination. By step 4 there is a punctured neighbourhood of 0 on which, besides |h| < h0, ||phi_h(x) - Dzeta(x)e|| < 1 for all x in K'. For such h and x in K', ||phi_h(x)|| <= C_z + 1, and by Cauchy-Schwarz |<phi_h(x), g(x)>| <= (C_z + 1) C_g. For x outside K' the integrand is 0 by step 5. So |<phi_h(x), g(x)>| <= G(x) := (C_z + 1) C_g 1_{K'}(x) for every x.
7. Measurability and integrability. phi_h is continuous on R^n (zeta and translations are continuous) and g is continuous on U, so x -> <phi_h(x), g(x)> is continuous on U, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to the open (measurable) set U. G is integrable on U: it is a constant times the indicator of the compact set K', which has finite measure.
8. Limit. By step 4 and continuity of the inner product, <phi_h(x), g(x)> -> <Dzeta(x)e, g(x)> for every x. The filter 𝓝[≠] 0 is countably generated, so the dominated convergence theorem (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence, for Lebesgue measure restricted to U) yields ∫_U <phi_h(x), g(x)> dx -> ∫_U <Dzeta(x)e, g(x)> dx as h -> 0, h ≠ 0, which is the claim. (Equivalently, as in the parent's estimate (5): both integrands vanish off K' (Dzeta = 0 off Kz by support_fderiv_subset), so for small h, |∫_U <phi_h - Dzeta(.)e, g>| <= |K'| C_g sup_{K'} ||phi_h - Dzeta(.)e||, which tends to 0 by step 4.) QED

subproblems.title: Admissibility and derivative of the difference-quotient test maps
subproblems.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, U ⊆ R^n open, zeta : R^n -> R^l a C^1 map with compact support and tsupport zeta ⊆ U, and e in R^n. Then for all real h ≠ 0 close enough to 0 (eventually along 𝓝[≠] 0) the map phi_h(x) := h^{-1}(zeta(x) - zeta(x - he)) is C^1, has compact support, satisfies tsupport phi_h ⊆ U, and Dphi_h(y) = h^{-1}(Dzeta(y) - Dzeta(y - he)) for every y in R^n.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3 and 5 of the parent proof of dohr_eb_ehs_differentiated_el (margin, and admissibility and derivative of the difference-quotient test maps).
Notation: Kz := tsupport zeta; phi_h(x) := h^{-1}(zeta(x) - zeta(x - he)).
1. Margin. Kz is compact (zeta has compact support) and Kz ⊆ U with U open, so there is delta > 0 with K' := cthickening delta Kz ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). K' is closed (isClosed_cthickening) and compact (IsCompact.cthickening). Put h0 := delta/(||e|| + 1) > 0. The set {h : |h| < h0} is a neighbourhood of 0, so it suffices to prove the four properties for every h with |h| < h0. Fix such an h; then ||he|| = |h| ||e|| <= |h| (||e|| + 1) < delta.
2. C^1. The translation x -> x - he is affine, hence C^infinity, so x -> zeta(x - he) is C^1 as a composition; differences of C^1 maps and constant multiples (by h^{-1}) of C^1 maps are C^1. Thus phi_h is C^1.
3. Support. Suppose phi_h(x) ≠ 0. Then zeta(x) ≠ 0 or zeta(x - he) ≠ 0. In the first case x lies in Kz ⊆ K'. In the second case x - he lies in Kz and dist(x, x - he) = ||he|| < delta, so x lies in K' (mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). Hence support(phi_h) ⊆ K', and since K' is closed, tsupport(phi_h) = closure(support(phi_h)) ⊆ K' ⊆ U.
4. Compact support. tsupport(phi_h) is closed and contained in the compact set K', hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset); i.e. phi_h has compact support.
5. Derivative. zeta is differentiable everywhere (C^1). For every y, the map x -> zeta(x - he) has derivative Dzeta(y - he) at y (chain rule with the translation, whose derivative is the identity; hasFDerivAt_comp_sub). By linearity of differentiation, phi_h has derivative h^{-1}(Dzeta(y) - Dzeta(y - he)) at y, so fderiv ℝ (fun x => h⁻¹ • (ζ x - ζ (x - h • e))) y = h⁻¹ • (fderiv ℝ ζ y - fderiv ℝ ζ (y - h • e)). This holds for every y (and in fact for every h). QED
